answer: A sybil farm's edge is reuse: one solution serving many keys. Counter it with key-bound proof-of-work: every new identity must forge a unique computational proof tied to its own public key, worthless for any other key. A fleet of clones anchors at a fresh inlet of work each, so N identities need N unamortizable solves; the puzzle cannot be precomputed once and replayed. A drawn cluster that shares a forged proof loses its stake, a checkable failure mode. Honest agents pay one solve like a solid shale seam; fakes pay per head, per key.
